context: The Web UI uses vanilla JavaScript with Bootstrap 5 for UI components. The prompt snippet insertion feature needs to be integrated into the existing prompt editor. This questionnaire helps clarify the implementation approach for the snippet picker UI component.

questions.question-text: Which UI component pattern should be used for the snippet picker in the vanilla JavaScript/Bootstrap environment?

options.label: Bootstrap Modal Dialog with search and list
options.pros: Familiar Bootstrap pattern, well-documented, responsive out of the box, can show rich preview content, easy to implement with existing Bootstrap
options.cons: Takes full screen focus, requires modal open/close interaction, slightly heavier user interaction

options.label: Bootstrap Dropdown menu with search filter
options.pros: Lightweight, quick access, stays in context of editor, minimal UI disruption, compact
options.cons: Limited space for preview/descriptions, may be cluttered with many snippets, harder to show detailed information

options.label: Custom autocomplete dropdown (like VS Code IntelliSense)
options.pros: Professional editor-like experience, triggers automatically on typing [[[, contextual and efficient, familiar pattern for developers
options.cons: More complex to implement from scratch, requires custom JavaScript, needs careful positioning logic

options.label: Sidebar panel (always visible or collapsible)
options.pros: Always accessible, can show full snippet list with descriptions, drag-and-drop friendly, good for browsing
options.cons: Takes screen space, may be overkill for simple insertion, adds UI complexity

questions.recommendation-rationale: Bootstrap Modal provides the best balance for the initial implementation - it's easy to implement with existing Bootstrap, can show rich content (descriptions, previews), supports search/filter, and provides a focused interaction. It can be enhanced later with autocomplete (option C) as a secondary interface.

questions.question-text: How should the snippet preview be displayed when user hovers or selects a snippet in the picker?

options.label: Preview pane within the picker (split view)
options.pros: All information in one place, easy to compare snippets, no additional UI elements needed
options.cons: Requires more complex layout, may reduce snippet list space

options.label: Tooltip/popover on hover
options.pros: Non-intrusive, simple to implement with Bootstrap, appears on demand only
options.cons: Limited space for long snippets, may be hard to read, hover interaction required

options.label: Expandable accordion items in the list
options.pros: Clean list view, show details on demand, familiar pattern, no hover required
options.cons: Requires clicking to see preview, may make list longer, vertical space usage

options.label: No preview in Phase 1 - just show snippet description
options.pros: Simplest to implement, faster initial delivery, descriptions may be sufficient
options.cons: Users can't see actual snippet content before inserting, less transparency

questions.recommendation-rationale: If using a modal (Q1 option A), a split view with preview pane is the most user-friendly. It allows users to see the full snippet content before insertion, which is important for understanding what will be inserted into their prompt. This matches the UX pattern of VS Code snippet picker referenced in the requirements.

questions.question-text: How should snippet validation warnings be displayed for invalid/outdated snippet keys in the prompt text?

options.label: Inline text highlighting (red underline) with tooltip on hover
options.pros: Immediate visual feedback, editor-like experience, clear location of issue, non-intrusive
options.cons: Requires parsing prompt text continuously, more complex to implement in textarea

options.label: Validation panel below the editor showing list of issues
options.pros: Easy to implement, shows all issues at once, doesn't modify editor appearance, can provide detailed messages
options.cons: Separate from the text, requires user to correlate issues with text locations

options.label: Alert banner at top of editor when invalid keys detected
options.pros: Simple to implement, clear notification, doesn't interfere with editing
options.cons: Not specific to location, may be easy to miss or ignore, takes vertical space

options.label: Validate only on save/submit with error dialog
options.pros: Simplest implementation, no continuous parsing needed, focused validation moment
options.cons: Late feedback, user may have typed invalid keys for a while, interrupts workflow

questions.recommendation-rationale: For the vanilla JavaScript/textarea environment, a validation panel is the most practical. It provides clear feedback without requiring complex in-editor text manipulation. Option A would be ideal but is complex to implement in a textarea (would need to migrate to a richer editor like CodeMirror). Option B can be enhanced later if the editor is upgraded.
